# BTY AI BOOT v1

**Status: LOCKED (BIOS)** — Do not edit except by explicit Commander decision.  
This file will not change with sprints or features. Same Boot in 6 months, same philosophy.

**The Operating Principles Behind BTY**

This document is the boot sequence for every AI participating in the BTY project.

It is **not** a product specification.  
It is **not** an implementation guide.  
It defines **how to think** before writing a single line of code.

Read [`BTY_PRODUCT_CONSTITUTION.md`](./BTY_PRODUCT_CONSTITUTION.md) **first** — belief before reasoning.  
Then read this file. Features live in code. **Purpose lives here.**

---

## 0. Protect the Constitution

Your first responsibility is not to build features.

Your first responsibility is to **protect the architecture**.

If implementation conflicts with the Constitution,  
**the implementation is wrong.**

→ Constitution: [`BTY_PRODUCT_CONSTITUTION.md`](./BTY_PRODUCT_CONSTITUTION.md)

---

## 1. BTY is a Culture Operating System

BTY is not a game.  
BTY is not a dashboard.  
BTY is not a learning platform.

BTY exists to **change real-world behavior** and **build organizational culture**.

Every feature must strengthen that purpose.

---

## 2. Reality is the Source

Reality creates growth.  
The application never creates growth.

The application only **observes, verifies, remembers, and reflects** reality.

```
Reality
  ↓
Verified Behavior
  ↓
Core XP
  ↓
Identity
  ↓
Avatar
```

Arena is a **reflection of reality**.  
Never the opposite.

---

## 3. Verified Reality is the Root

The permanent value inside BTY is **Core XP**.  
Everything else is derived.

```
Core XP
  ↓
Avatar
  ↓
Identity
  ↓
Codes
  ↓
Stages
  ↓
TII
  ↓
Leaderboards
  ↓
Weekly views
```

Nothing bypasses Core XP.

---

## 4. Reality Engines

Reality enters BTY through **Reality Engines**.

Examples today:

- **Action Engine** — verified commitments in the real world
- **Reality Event Engine** — verified participation in real events
- **Learning Engine** — verified learning in the real world *(next)*

Future engines follow the same pattern.

Every Reality Engine follows one contract:

```
award()
  ↓
new_core_xp
  ↓
reproject(new_core_xp)
```

Reality Engines **never calculate growth**.  
They only **verify reality** and **award Core XP**.

Growth is computed **after** Core XP is confirmed — never before.

---

## 5. QR is a Verification Language

QR is not the product.  
QR is not the goal.

QR is the **language used to verify reality**.

Without verification, there is no trusted growth.

---

## 6. Architecture Before Features

Never improve a page simply because it looks imperfect.

Always ask:

> *Will this page survive the final architecture?*

If the answer is no,  
stop polishing it.

Build the **final resident** instead.

---

## 7. Today is the Home

The center of BTY is not a dashboard.  
It is **TODAY**.

TODAY answers only one question:

> *What should I do in the real world today?*

Everything else is secondary.

TODAY eventually becomes:

- **ACTION**
- **EVENT**
- **LEARNING**

All roads return to TODAY.

---

## 8. One Permanent Identity

Avatar is not decoration.  
Avatar is **visualized verified growth**.

Identity must always be **earned**.  
Never fabricated.

---

## 9. Culture Before Gamification

People should never perform actions merely to earn points.

Points exist to **recognize meaningful actions that already matter**.

The culture comes first.  
The gamification comes second.

---

## 10. Minimize Complexity

Do not introduce a new screen,  
new navigation,  
new engine,  
new table,  
or new architecture

unless it creates **permanent value**.

The simplest architecture that preserves the Constitution is almost always correct.

---

## 11. Build Systems, Not Features

Never ask:

> *What feature should we build?*

Instead ask:

> *What system does this belong to?*

Features disappear.  
Systems survive.

---

## 12. The Final Question

Before every implementation, ask one question:

> *Does this make BTY bring people back into reality?*

If the answer is no,  
it does not belong in BTY.

That question overrides every design decision.

---
